name: Exp1 early-stop (unparseable generation) diagnosis
status: diagnostic record only — no model output, evaluation, or result was altered
what_happened: Some claude-opus-5 generations terminate mid-token: the response ends inside an identifier or call (e.g. 'return y_inter', 'datetime.timedelta(days=3') and the opening code fence is never closed. The file is therefore not parseable and scores as a failure.

where_it_bites.other_models: gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.4-mini have 0-1 unparseable outputs per condition; deepseek-v4-flash-0731 has up to 10 under skeleton_holistic.

correlate: For claude-opus-5 the unclosed-fence count equals the syntax-failure count almost exactly (32/32 in the formal run). The 368 parseable outputs are 343 closed / 25 unclosed; all 32 unparseable outputs are unclosed. This makes 'unterminated code fence' a reliable marker for the failure mode in this arm only — models that never emit fences (gpt-5.4) show 100/100 'unclosed' but 0 syntax failures, so the marker is not comparable across arms.
timing: Unparseable responses finish fast (median 5.8s, 762 output tokens) versus parseable ones (median 9.0s, 1360 output tokens), so this is not a max_tokens exhaustion: the 4096-token cap is never approached.
controls_run: Re-issuing the identical prompt reproduces a cut at approximately the same place (ClassEval_46/spl_only: 351, 377, 333, 315 chars over 3 attempts).
Raising max_tokens to 8192 does not help; thinking=disabled does not help; appending 'Output the complete Python class.' does not help.
The SAME prompt truncates other models too: gpt-5.4 produced 1491 chars unclosed after 93s. So this is prompt-content-triggered, not a claude-opus-5 or gateway defect.
claude-opus-5 can produce long outputs: a request for 40 classes returned 6022 output tokens / 8265 chars with a closed fence, so there is no hard ceiling.
reporting_rule: Report the raw 100-denominator figures as the official result — the frozen protocol scores an unparseable file as a failure. The excluding-unparseable figures are an upper bound for interpretation only and must be labelled as such.
rejected_remedy: A retry-until-parseable recovery was run and then fully reverted: it would have changed the sampling protocol relative to the other five arms, so it is not part of the result. All affected output.txt files were restored byte-for-byte and no evaluation was re-run against recovered outputs.
probe_scripts: $PROJECT_ROOT/scripts/recover_early_stop_outputs.py (written, then reverted; kept as a diagnostic tool only)
